title: uchar-ir-v1
description: Structural schema for the 'uchar-ir-v1' format in its L5 shape (spec/proposals/V1-WIREMIGRATIE.md, section 7, landings L1 to L5): the former 'regelspraak-ir-v0' dump of the reference frontend's fully resolved model with its CONTAINER restructured (L1), its REFERENCE LAYER reduced to the symbolic form (L2), its TYPE SYSTEM in the v1 nodes (L3), its RULE AND EXPRESSION LAYER in the v1 forms (L4), and its SOURCE TEXTS in the source record and its NAMES in the spelling of IR-SPEC (L5). The root nests {format, model, rules, diagnostics} (decision V3 (b)): 'model' is the declaration set of IR-SPEC ch. 2, as lists in declaration order (WF-019), with no map keys; 'rules' carries one list per rule-form kind, in the order of IR-SPEC ch. 2 (Rules), the single-source and union uniqueness forms in the one list 'uniquenesses'; 'diagnostics' is the producer's own account (WF-113). An ObjectType carries its members as Attribute and Characteristic nodes with their own facets (TimelineFacet), and a Domain wraps a name and a datatype that carries no self-name at the declaration position (domainDatatype). A reference carries only its symbolic form (L2): the five reference classes carry no type annotation, because the declaration is the one source; an attribute reference names its navigation by role bindings alone; the range of an instance fold, a quantifier fold and an allocation is written, never derived; one RoleMembership node names the fact type and the role the subject fills; a fact creation and a scoped uniqueness carry their symbolic fields alone; and the datatype union has no member for an unknown type (B16). The type system is the v1 one (L3): a number is a Number, and a percentage a Number with the unit '%' that carries the presentation tag 'percentage' at a declaration (B14); a date is one Date node with its precision (B15); a unit is a Unit whose conversion factor is an exact rational {num, den} (B17 (i)) and whose declaration carries its spellings; a unit system is a list of units; a day kind is a DayKind node with its plural; and a parameter carries the attribute's timeline facet without a timeline name (B18). The rule and expression layer is the v1 one (L4): each of the six named forms (Rule, Allocation, ObjectCreation, FactCreation, Consistency, Uniqueness) is {node, name, versions}, its version records carrying no node discriminator (B19); a rule version carries the 'initialisation' flag and, on a computing version, the dialect tag 'presentation', and whether it writes an attribute or a characteristic is its target's declaration (B20); a uniqueness names its sources, one or more (B27); a fact creation reaches its target along a 'path' of role bindings; an aggregation and a builtin call are two nodes, each with its own fields (B21); a literal carries a typed value in the variants of the case format, a decimal point where the source wrote a comma (B22); and the bound day of a day-kind definition and the two session values are BoundDay and ContextValue (B23). Every source text is in the source record (B26): the optional field 'source' (sourceReference: a non-empty 'snippet', and 'line' where a consistency version or a rule group has one) stands where the v0 field 'bron' stood, on every node that carried one, and is required on an Unresolved marker; a node without source text carries none. Every node, field and enum value carries its IR-SPEC name (B6, B10), the enum values in the spelling of IR-SPEC's Conventions (English, lowerCamel), and a field IR-SPEC names optional is absent rather than null on the renamed nodes; the one exception is the rule-status check, which keeps its v0 node Regelversie with its fields regel and inconsistent until its v1 form lands (B25). The optional list 'vocabularies' after 'format' declares the named vocabularies of IR-SPEC ch. 2.12, and the optional field 'designations' on the designatable declarations, and 'valueDesignations' on an enumeration's declaration, carry the designations: a side table without semantics, read structurally by every reader and for evaluation by none, whose content rules are the verifier's (WF-116 to WF-120); each of the two fields stands last on its node. The optional field 'origin', on the same declarations and just before 'designations', carries the origin of a declaration a producer made itself (IR-SPEC ch. 2.13): a side table without semantics in the same discipline, whose content rules are the verifier's (WF-121). The optional field 'anchor', with the one value 'form', on an AttributeReference (after subjectType), a CharacteristicCheck (after host), an Aggregation and a QuantifierFold (after elementType), and the condition node IdentityCheck, carry the form anchor of IR-SPEC ch. 4.1a: in the filter of an instance fold or of a union selection, or in the filter or the test of a quantifier fold, where the subject is the element, a node with the anchor reads the subject of the form, and an identity check compares the element with it; where the two may stand is the verifier's (WF-122). Canonical key order is the 'properties' order of this schema: the migration script and every emitter write exactly that order, and every node no landing restructured keeps the order its v0 emitter wrote, less the keys L2 removed, with its keys renamed in place. Every object is closed (additionalProperties:false) and lists every always-emitted key as required; node subtypes are discriminated on the 'node' field. Exception, by the decided wire-entry discipline (IR-SPEC, Method): extension fields carrying v1 deltas (connectingRole on an object creation, the fold ranges sourceRole and sourcePath on an Aggregation and a QuantifierFold, and statuteAnnotations — of each range pair the second is the multi-step fold-source range of IR-SPEC ch. 4.3 / WF-102, two or more RoleBindings subject-outwards and mutually exclusive with the first, which is the one-step spelling of the same field; and statuteAnnotations carries the statute annotations on a Rule, when present a non-empty list of non-empty strings and absent otherwise) are optional where L2 makes none of them required (the allocation's connectingRole and the range of a fold and of a quantifier fold, under the conditions stated on those nodes), the datatype union admits the extension nodes SumType (the payload-carrying variant family, CONSTRUCTS row 36), ListType (the sequence type, CONSTRUCTS row 10) and StructType (the record datatype, spec/proposals/PHASE5C-TUTORIAL.md §2), the expr union admits the extension nodes TemporalRead, Construct, Match, BinderRef, StructLiteral, FieldAccess, the row-10 fold family (ListLiteral, Lambda, IfThenElse, Invoke, Fold, MapList, FilterList, ListLength) and the value-level binding Let (spec/proposals/PHASE5C-TUTORIAL.md §6), and the optional lists functionDefs (under 'model') and prioritizedDefaults (under 'rules') carry the named-logic and prioritized-defaults extensions, and a Default carries the optional exceptions field — its nested exception groups (RUNTIME-SEMANTICS ch. 7.9) — the v0 emitter produces none of them EXCEPT Let and BinderRef, which the RegelSpraak frontend has emitted for a §13.4.2.10 variabelendeel since the let-lowering card (2026-09-01); when present they are all written whole, never null. Wire epoch v0.10 (the rename epoch, 2026-08-29): the prioritized-defaults spellings (prioritizedDefaults/Default/ExceptionGroup and the defaults list) are the only valid ones; a file in the pre-rename spelling (see the formerly notes, IR-SPEC ch. 6.1 and RUNTIME-SEMANTICS ch. 7.1) fails loudly against the closed objects. Section citations (e.g. §13.3.3) point into the source language spec by number only.

vocabularies.description: Extension list (IR-SPEC ch. 2.12): the named vocabularies the designations of this document are written in. Optional, written whole or not at all: absent when the document declares none, and when present at least one. Like every designation, a side table without semantics: every reader reads it structurally, and none reads it for evaluation.

model.description: The model layer: the declaration set of IR-SPEC ch. 2. The six former v0 registries are lists in declaration order, each entry carrying its name on its node (there is no map key); the timelines were a list in v0 already; the day kinds are a list of DayKind nodes, each carrying its own spellings (L3). functionDefs is an extension list: optional, written whole or not at all.

functionDefs.description: Extension list (v1, CONSTRUCTS row 10): named reusable logic (FunctionDef) per spec/IR-SPEC.md ch. 2.11. Optional; the v0 emitter never produces it.

rules.description: The rule layer: one list per rule-form kind, in the order of IR-SPEC ch. 2 (Rules); the lists carried their v0 keys until L5. Since L4 the six named forms are in their v1 shape (IR-SPEC ch. 3, Versioning): each entry is one form with its versions, and the single-source and union uniqueness forms share the one list uniquenesses (delta B27; the migration and the emitters write the single-source forms first, then the unions, each in v0 order). prioritizedDefaults is an extension list: optional, written whole or not at all.

prioritizedDefaults.description: Extension list (v1, Phase 4): prioritized-defaults groups (characteristic and attribute forms) per spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 7. Optional; the v0 emitter never produces it.

Number.description: A number (IR-SPEC ch. 2.4). 'whole' and 'decimals' carry the precision form; which combinations are well-formed is WF-007, a verifier check, so the schema admits any integer for 'decimals'. 'sign' is always written; a number declared without a sign is unspecified. 'unit' absent: the number carries no unit. A percentage is a Number whose unit is '%' (or a rate with '%' as its numerator), delta B14 of spec/proposals/V1-WIREMIGRATIE.md and CONSTRUCTS row 27; 'presentation' is its dialect(regelspraak) presentation tag, the one value 'percentage', written only at a declaration position (the datatype of an attribute, a parameter or a domain, a sum-type payload, a list element, a struct field, a function or lambda parameter, a function result) and never on a type annotation, where the verifier refuses it (WF-007). The tag carries no meaning for evaluation. Key order is this 'properties' order.

Date.description: A date (IR-SPEC ch. 2.4; delta B15 of spec/proposals/V1-WIREMIGRATIE.md): one node, parameterised by its precision. 'day' and 'millisecond' share no order (WF-036), so the precision is always written.

SumType.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node SumType, never emitter-produced): the payload-carrying variant family of CONSTRUCTS row 36 — a declared, nominal sum type, declared as a Domain in 'model.domains' (there without its 'domain' self-name: DomainSumType) and repeated whole at every use site. Each constructor carries a 'name' and either one 'payload' datatype (unary) or null (nullary). See spec/IR-SPEC.md ch. 2.4 (WF-060/061).

ListType.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node ListType, never emitter-produced): an ordered, possibly empty sequence type of CONSTRUCTS row 10. 'element' is the single element datatype (first-order and non-list — WF-065). See spec/IR-SPEC.md ch. 2.4 (WF-065).

StructType.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node StructType, never emitter-produced): the record datatype of the Phase-5c core (spec/proposals/PHASE5C-TUTORIAL.md §2) — a declared, nominal record, declared as a Domain in 'model.domains' (there without its 'domain' self-name: DomainStructType) and repeated whole at every use site, exactly the SumType/ListType landing pattern. Each field carries a 'name' and a non-null 'datatype' (a number, day-precision date, sum type or struct type — WF-071). See spec/IR-SPEC.md ch. 2.4 (WF-071/072).

domainDatatype.description: The datatype at the DECLARATION position, Domain.datatype (IR-SPEC ch. 2.3). It admits the same datatype nodes as 'datatype', except that Enumeration, SumType and StructType appear here in a form without their self-name field 'domain': the Domain wrapper carries the name, and a second spelling of it cannot be written. At every REFERENCE position (attributes, parameters, expressions, payloads, fields, elements) the 'datatype' union applies unchanged: there that field is the domain reference of IR-SPEC ch. 2.4 (WF-003), not a self-name, and stays required. The three declaration forms share their remaining field schemas with the reference forms by JSON pointer, so each field is defined once.

DomainEnumeration.description: Enumeration at the declaration position of a Domain: the 'domain' self-name is absent (see domainDatatype); 'values' is the reference form's own field schema. 'valueDesignations' is the extension field of IR-SPEC ch. 2.12, the designations of the values, written whole or not at all and only here: an enumeration value is a bare string on the wire, so its designations stand beside the list it is declared in, and a use site, which repeats the values, carries none.

DomainSumType.description: SumType at the declaration position of a Domain: the 'domain' self-name is absent (see domainDatatype); 'constructors' is the reference form's own field schema.

DomainStructType.description: StructType at the declaration position of a Domain: the 'domain' self-name is absent (see domainDatatype); 'fields' is the reference form's own field schema.

Unit.description: A unit where it occurs (IR-SPEC ch. 2.5): on a Number, and as the denominator of a rate. 'abbreviation' is its primary spelling. 'system' names the declaring UnitSystem (WF-034 (r)); it is absent for the built-in '%' and for the bare calendar units. 'canonical' and 'factorToCanonical' are the conversion pair, both present or both absent (WF-092). The factor is an exact positive rational, how many canonical units equal one of this unit, written {num, den} without a node discriminator (delta B17 (i) of spec/proposals/V1-WIREMIGRATIE.md, CONSTRUCTS row 26); that it is in lowest terms is a verifier check (WF-092), because a schema cannot state a greatest common divisor. 'denominator' is the denominator unit of a rate. No field is ever null: absent is the one spelling of a field not given. A unit's further spellings belong to its declaration (DeclaredUnit), so an occurrence cannot carry them. Key order is this 'properties' order.

DeclaredUnit.description: A unit as its UnitSystem declares it (IR-SPEC ch. 2.5): the node of Unit, and after its fields 'spellings', the further spellings that resolve to this unit (word and plural aliases), at least one when present. Only the declaration carries them: an occurrence of the unit is a Unit, which has no such field, so a spelling written there cannot be accepted and dropped. The other fields are Unit's own field schemas, by JSON pointer, so each is defined once. Key order is this 'properties' order.

sourceReference.description: The structured source reference (IR-SPEC ch. 4; delta B26): the record under the key 'source' on every node that carries source text. It carries no node discriminator: on the wire it is a field of its node, not a node. 'snippet' is the node's source text, byte for byte as the producer wrote it, and never empty: a node without source text carries no source. 'line' (at least 1) is the line of the source text; the migration and the emitters write it on a consistency version and a rule group alone. The positions 'file' and 'column' are not admitted until the card that first writes positions fixes their conventions.

Literal.description: A literal (IR-SPEC ch. 4.1): a typed value, not a lexeme (delta B22). 'value' is exactly one variant of the value union of uchar-case-v0, the variant being the one 'type' names (a verifier rule: one datatype union serves every literal, so the schema cannot cross the two). A number is an exact decimal string with a point, or a rational a/b, never a JSON number; the author's spelling, a decimal comma included, stays in the snippet of the source record 'source'. 'type' is nullable: a typeless value node is WF-034's, with its own witness.

LiteralValue.description: The value of a Literal: exactly one variant, carried over from the 'value' union of uchar-case-v0 with its patterns, without the list and struct variants (no literal carries one) and without a constructor payload (a literal names a constructor, it does not apply one). The patterns are shape tests: that a date is a calendar day and that the variant is the one the literal's type names are verifier rules with their own witnesses.

text.description: The string between the source delimiters.

anchor.description: The form anchor (IR-SPEC ch. 4.1a, WF-122): the range starts at the subject of the form instead of the element, where the fold stands in a per-element context; the fold's own filter moves the subject to its element again, and its emptyFallback reads on the form subject. Absent: the range starts at the subject of its position.

Aggregation.description: An aggregation (IR-SPEC ch. 4.3): the eight fold kinds, with only the fields a fold carries (delta B21); an absent optional field is none. The RANGE of an instance fold is written, never derived (delta B12; CONSTRUCTS row 4): with an elementType, exactly one argument and a kind other than total, exactly one of sourceRole (the one-step range) and sourcePath (the multi-step range, WF-102) is present. A total without either is the subject's own read over its own attribute (the verifier holds that it is, WF-083), and no fold carries both. With two or more arguments the node is the listed value fold, whose operands are ordinary reads: it has no range, whatever elementType it carries. Which kind admits emptyFallback and dimensionSelection is WF-037's.

BuiltinCall.description: A builtin call (IR-SPEC ch. 4.3): the seventeen scalar, text and date builtins, with plain arguments and only the fields a builtin carries (delta B21): no element type, range, empty fallback or dimension selection, which are an Aggregation's. 'granularity' is the bucket and 'filter' the condition of timeProportionalPart and dayCount; which kind requires or admits them is WF-037's and WF-056's.

Clamp.description: A clamp (IR-SPEC ch. 4.2): 'base' bounded below by 'minimum' and above by 'maximum'; an absent bound is no bound on that side.

anchor.description: The form anchor (IR-SPEC ch. 4.1a, WF-122): the read starts at the subject of the form instead of the element, where it stands in a per-element context (the filter of an instance fold or of a union selection, the filter or the test of a quantifier fold). Without a path it is the form subject's own read, and its subjectType is the form subject type (WF-053); with one, the path walks from the form subject. Absent: the read starts at the subject of its position.

path.description: The navigation hops as symbolic role bindings, subject-outward, one binding per hop — the bound role is the role the hop reaches (the far role). Present exactly when the reference reads off the subject: a reference without it is the subject's own read, whose subjectType is the subject type (WF-053); the zero-hop self-reference of IR-SPEC ch. 4.1a is such a read. Written whole or not at all, never null.

ContextValue.description: A session value (IR-SPEC ch. 4.1; delta B23): 'name' is the evaluation date evaluationDate or the evaluation year evaluationYear, in that spelling. The schema leaves the name a free string on purpose: the name set is closed and crossed byte for byte by WF-098, which gives a name outside it a witness of its own, 'de dag' and the v0 spelling 'Rekendatum' included (the bound day is BoundDay).

BoundDay.description: The bound day of a day-kind definition (IR-SPEC ch. 3.7 and 4.1; delta B23): the day the definition is about, not a session value. It carries no name. Outside a day-kind definition it denotes nothing, and every executor faults on it by name (RUNTIME-SEMANTICS ch. 3.8).

ExprUnresolved.description: An expression the resolver could not resolve; surfaces as an explicit marker. 'type' is optional: absent means the type is unknown, present it is a real datatype, never null. 'source' is required: a marker is accounted for by the diagnostic that quotes its snippet (WF-113 (b)).

TemporalRead.description: Extension node (v1, CONSTRUCTS row 11): the point-in-time read read(tl, d) of spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 3.3. Never emitter-produced; base, date and type are required and non-null.

Construct.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node Construct, never emitter-produced): builds a sum-type constructor value (CONSTRUCTS row 36; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 9.1). 'argument' is an expr iff the constructor is unary, null for a nullary constructor. 'type' (the SumType) is required and non-null.

Match.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node Match, never emitter-produced): deconstructs a sum-type value, one arm per declared constructor (CONSTRUCTS row 36; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 9.2). A unary arm carries a 'binder' name, a nullary arm carries null. 'type' (the result datatype) and 'scrutinee' are required and non-null.

BinderRef.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node BinderRef, EMITTER-PRODUCED since the let-lowering card, 2026-09-01): reads the nearest enclosing binder of its name — a match arm's, a lambda/function parameter, or a Let binder (CONSTRUCTS rows 36 and 24; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 9.2 / ch. 10.6). The RegelSpraak emitter produces one for every read of a §13.4.2.10 variabele in a rule's result part. Deliberately distinct from VariableReference, which since that card survives only as the residual marker for a variable the resolver could NOT bind (row 24). 'name' is required and non-null; the read carries no type of its own, the binder's declaration is the one source (B13).

StructLiteral.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node StructLiteral, never emitter-produced): builds a record value (spec/proposals/PHASE5C-TUTORIAL.md §2; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 11). 'fields' supplies exactly the declared fields, each once, in declaration order — WF-073; a field whose value evaluates leeg propagates (the whole literal is leeg, the no-hole rule). 'type' (the StructType) is required and non-null.

FieldAccess.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node FieldAccess, never emitter-produced): reads one declared field of a record (spec/proposals/PHASE5C-TUTORIAL.md §2; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 11). 'base' is struct-typed and 'field' is one of its declared fields; the node 'type' is that field's datatype — WF-074. A leeg base propagates. 'type' and 'base' are required and non-null.

Lambda.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node Lambda, never emitter-produced): a typed anonymous function (CONSTRUCTS row 10; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 10). Position-restricted to the 'function' operand of Fold/MapList — WF-069 (not a schema concern); its 'body' is closed. Carries no 'type': a lambda is never a value.

ListLiteral.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node ListLiteral, never emitter-produced): an ordered list value (CONSTRUCTS row 10; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 10.1). Every element carries the declared element datatype of 'type' (a ListType) — WF-066. 'type' is required and non-null.

IfThenElse.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node IfThenElse, never emitter-produced): a value-level conditional (CONSTRUCTS row 10; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 10.2). Position-restricted to lambda and function bodies — WF-069 (not a schema concern); the guard reuses the condition union; both branches agree on 'type'. 'type', 'condition', 'then' and 'else' are required and non-null.

Invoke.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node Invoke, never emitter-produced): calls a FunctionDef by name (CONSTRUCTS row 10; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 10.2). Arity, argument and result typing: WF-068. 'type' is required and non-null.

Fold.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node Fold, never emitter-produced): the left fold (CONSTRUCTS row 10; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 10.2). 'function' is a two-parameter (accumulator, element) Lambda; a bare FunctionDef name is structurally valid on the wire but WF-069 requires the inline Lambda (a named function reaches a fold through a lambda body that Invokes it). The accumulator/init/body/type share one first-order non-list datatype — WF-070. 'type', 'list' and 'init' are required and non-null.

MapList.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node MapList, never emitter-produced): the order-preserving map (CONSTRUCTS row 10; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 10.2). 'function' is a one-parameter Lambda; a bare FunctionDef name is structurally valid on the wire but WF-069 requires the inline Lambda (a named function reaches a map through a lambda body that Invokes it). 'type' (a ListType) is the ListType of the body's datatype — WF-070. 'type' and 'list' are required and non-null.

FilterList.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node FilterList, never emitter-produced): keeps the elements whose 'condition' holds with 'binder' bound to the element (CONSTRUCTS row 10; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 10.2) — the aggregation-filter precedent (a binder plus a condition, never a boolean-bodied lambda). 'type' (the source ListType) equals the source's type — WF-070. 'type', 'list' and 'condition' are required and non-null.

ListLength.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node ListLength, never emitter-produced): the element count (CONSTRUCTS row 10; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 10.2). 'type' is a whole Number — WF-070. 'type' and 'list' are required and non-null.

Let.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node Let, EMITTER-PRODUCED since the let-lowering card, 2026-09-01): the value-level binding (spec/proposals/PHASE5C-TUTORIAL.md §6, question 2 = A; spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 10.6). The RegelSpraak frontend lowers a §13.4.2.10 variabelendeel ('Daarbij geldt: ...') to one Let per declared variable that the rule's RESULT part reads, nested in declaration order (§11.1 rule 1, first-declared outermost); a variable read only in the voorwaarde is substituted at its use site instead, because no expr node can span the separate 'condition' and 'value' wire fields of a rule version. 'binder' is visible only in 'body', never in its own 'value' — WF-076; it joins the WF-064 binder regime. The node 'type' equals the 'body' type — WF-076. Call-by-need (maintainer decision O3, 2026-09-01): the 'value' is evaluated in the enclosing scope at the FIRST read of the binder and reused for every further read; a read whose 'value' evaluates leeg makes the WHOLE Let leeg (the leeg-barrier, at the read place), so a body binder is never leeg — which is what carries the WF-069 widening (IfThenElse becomes admissible inside Let bodies) and the WF-077 condition-operand discipline; a binder the body never reads is never evaluated at all (no leeg, no fault, no channel fact) and the body's outcome is the Let's. 'type', 'binder', 'value' and 'body' are required and non-null.

InstanceSetBranch.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node InstanceSetBranch): one selection of an InstanceSetUnion — an element type, the one-step relation the selection ranges over, and an optional die/dat subselection evaluated PER CONTRIBUTOR. 'elementType' is carried nullable so a missing one is a WF-110 violation the verifier REPORTS with its rule, never a load failure; 'sourceRole' is required and non-null, because the selection's relation is written and nothing derives it (B12). There is deliberately no path spelling here: the multi-step range under a count is WF-102's and this node does not reopen it.

InstanceSetUnion.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node InstanceSetUnion, EMITTER-PRODUCED): the §5.7 concatenation of subject expressions as a set of INSTANCES — the source of an instance count (CONSTRUCTS row 1; spec/IR-SPEC.md ch. 4.3, semantics spec/RUNTIME-SEMANTICS.md ch. 3.4d). It carries no 'type': it denotes instances, not a value, so there is no annotation to twist and none to believe. Admissible ONLY as the single argument of an Aggregation of kind count, with at least two branches, and the count carrying it names no source of its own — WF-110. The members are the UNION of the branches' contributors, deduplicated on instance identity.

FunctionDef.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node FunctionDef, never emitter-produced): named reusable logic — DMN's Business Knowledge Model (CONSTRUCTS row 10; spec/IR-SPEC.md ch. 2.11). Carried by the optional 'functionDefs' list under 'model'. Ci-unique names, typed unique parameters, a resolvable 'result', a closed 'body', and an acyclic invocation graph: WF-067.

TextCompositionPart.description: A part of a text sequence: a literal fragment or an interpolated expression.

anchor.description: The form anchor (IR-SPEC ch. 4.1a, WF-122): the check reads the subject of the form instead of the element, where it stands in a per-element context; a check with the anchor carries no host (WF-122 (b)). Absent: the check reads the subject of its position, or its host.

navigation.description: The one navigation hop of a navigated characteristic check as a symbolic role binding — the bound role is the role the hop reaches, and the characteristic lives on the type it reaches. Absent: the check reads the subject itself (IR-SPEC ch. 4.1a and ch. 4.5). Written whole or not at all, never null.

RoleMembership.description: The role check (IR-SPEC ch. 4.5): true iff a link of the declared fact type 'factType' exists in which the subject fills 'role', named by its declared name, and whose other role is filled by an instance of 'counterpartType'; 'negated': no such link exists. 'counterpartType' is optional: absent, the other role's declared filler type is meant; present, it names a declared object type that is a subtype of, or equal to, the declared filler type of the other role (WF-034, IR-SPEC ch. 4.6 (o)); the migration and the emitter write the field only where it narrows (the L2 card, backlog/done/20260923-l2-referentielaag.md, U12). One node for both directions of the check (delta B9 of spec/proposals/V1-WIREMIGRATIE.md; CONSTRUCTS row 5); its key order is this 'properties' order.

quantifier.description: The quantifier over the instance range. all = every contributor satisfies 'test'; none = none does; the three counting forms compare the NUMBER of contributors that satisfy it with 'threshold' (atLeast: count >= threshold; atMost: count <= threshold; exactly: count == threshold). The vocabulary is Compound's, over instances instead of parts. the is NOT admitted here: the bare definite describes ONE member and is not a quantification over a set (WF-108 (a) refuses a hand-written one by name).

threshold.description: The counting quantifier's threshold — Compound's field, under Compound's rule (WF-041: at least 1). Written EXACTLY under atLeast / atMost / exactly and omitted under all / none, which is where this node diverges from Compound (there the field is written under every quantifier and read only under the three counting ones): a field that is meaningful in one position and inert everywhere else can say anything. The conditional below is the wire half of WF-108 (e); the verifier cites the rule.

elementType.description: The instance type quantified over — the POPULATION, extensionally (IR-SPEC ch. 2.2): the contributors are the instances the range reaches whose type is the subtype-or-equal of this one.

anchor.description: The form anchor (IR-SPEC ch. 4.1a, WF-122): the range starts at the subject of the form instead of the element, where the quantifier stands in a per-element context; its own filter and test move the subject to its element again. Absent: the range starts at the subject of its position.

filter.description: The die/dat subselection, evaluated PER CONTRIBUTOR with the element as subject — the same field, the same reading and the same machinery as Aggregation.filter (RUNTIME-SEMANTICS ch. 3.4a). It selects WHICH members are quantified over; 'test' is what each selected member must satisfy. Absent: no subselection.

test.description: The quantified matrix, evaluated PER CONTRIBUTOR with the element as subject. Nullable on the wire so a missing matrix is a citable WF-108 (d) violation rather than a load failure with no rule to name.

sourceRole.description: Extension field (wire-entry discipline, IR-SPEC Method): the one-step range — the connecting relation with the role whose filler instances the quantifier RANGES OVER bound. Spelled exactly as Aggregation.sourceRole. Exactly one of sourceRole and sourcePath is present: the range is written, never derived (B12). Never null.

sourcePath.description: Extension field (wire-entry discipline, IR-SPEC Method): the MULTI-STEP range, the relations walked subject-outwards, each step spelled exactly as sourceRole is. Two or more steps; the one-step range IS sourceRole and the two fields are mutually exclusive (WF-108 (c), the WF-102 discipline under this node's own rule).

QuantifierFold.description: Extension node (IR-SPEC Method; wire node QuantifierFold): the QUANTIFIER FOLD — first-order quantification of a condition over the members of a linked instance set (IR-SPEC ch. 4.5; RUNTIME-SEMANTICS ch. 3.9a). The first-order sibling of Compound, which quantifies over PARTS of one subject; this one quantifies over INSTANCES, and takes its range fields from the instance fold (ch. 4.3) unchanged.

anchor.description: The object the element is compared with: the subject of the form (IR-SPEC ch. 4.1a). Required, with this one value.

IdentityCheck.description: The identity check (IR-SPEC ch. 4.5, WF-122): true iff the subject of its position, the element of the filter or the test around it, is the same object as the subject of the form; 'negated' turns that around. It stands only where a form anchor stands (WF-122 (c)), reads no value, and draws no dependency edge (IR-SPEC ch. 5.1). Its key order is this 'properties' order.

Regelversie.description: The rule-status check (IR-SPEC ch. 4.5, RuleStatusCheck): the wire keeps its v0 node Regelversie with its v0 fields regel and inconsistent until the v1 form lands (B25); its source text is in 'source' since L5.

ConditionUnresolved.description: A condition the resolver could not resolve; surfaces as an explicit marker. 'source' is required: a marker is accounted for by the diagnostic that quotes its snippet (WF-113 (b)).

WholePeriod.description: The whole-period qualifier (IR-SPEC ch. 4.5): 'granularity' is the period the qualifier spans, year or month, and 'negated' negates it. It stands in the optional field 'wholePeriod' of a Comparison, a Predicate and a CharacteristicCheck; an absent 'wholePeriod' is no qualifier.

Validity.description: A validity window; 'from'/'to' are strict ISO dates (four-two-two digit fields, digits only, no sign and no extended year — WF-084's date-literal grammar, IR-SPEC ch. 4.1), and an absent bound is open-ended: a Validity with neither bound is always. The pattern is load-bearing, not decoration: the verifier holds a bound as an OPAQUE STRING and orders it lexicographically for WF-021's overlap check (which states the assumption in as many words), and that ordering is sound only inside this lexeme. The interpreter and the ASP backend held bounds the same way until 2026-09-23; since then they read the evaluation date and both bounds through the strict date reader, compare day numbers and refuse a non-date naming its position. Measured 2026-09-11 without the pattern: '+012026-01-01' as a bound made the interpreter and the ASP backend apply a rule version that the Drools backend, which parses the lexeme, did not — one document, two answers — while 'niet-een-datum' passed every reader in the house. A pattern cannot check the calendar; '2026-02-30' matches here and is refused one field deeper, by WF-101 in the verifier and by each executor's date reader.

ObjectType.description: An object type (IR-SPEC ch. 2.2). Since M1 each attribute and characteristic is a node carrying its own facets; v0 carried those facets in eight side-maps keyed by member name, so a facet without a member can no longer be written. 'plural' absent = none declared.

supertype.description: The single direct parent, by declared name; absent = a root type. An extension field under the Method's discipline: optional, never required, never null, written whole or not at all. The type is a bare string and NOT an array on purpose (IR-SPEC ch. 2.2, WF-106): single parenthood holds by wire SHAPE, so a second direct parent is not a document the verifier rejects but one that cannot be written — this closed node refuses the array form here, which is where that refusal is enforced. The cost is stated rather than hidden: WF-106 therefore carries no verifier check and no corpus/negative witness, and its witnesses live in the frontends that read the language above this wire.

Attribute.description: An attribute of an ObjectType (IR-SPEC ch. 2.2), in declaration order. 'plural' absent = none declared; 'dimensions' absent = scalar; when present it is non-empty (minItems 1, WF-004), so a scalar attribute has one spelling; 'timeline' absent = not time-dependent. 'datatype' admits null exactly as the v0 attribute map did: a datatype-less attribute is a loadable document, and the verifier refuses it (WF-059).

Characteristic.description: A characteristic of an ObjectType (IR-SPEC ch. 2.2), in declaration order. 'kind' is the presentation tag and is always written; a characteristic untagged in v0 is nominal. 'timeline' absent = not time-dependent.

TimelineFacet.description: The time-dependence of one member (IR-SPEC ch. 2.2). 'granularity' is required and non-null, so a facet without a grid cannot be written. 'count' is always written (1 = single-period). That it is at least 1 is WF-005, a verifier check, so the schema admits any integer here. 'fixedStart' is the timeline's own field, by JSON pointer (IR-SPEC ch. 2.8): an inline declaration carries its start point here, and a facet that names a timeline carries that timeline's (WF-115). 'timelineName' is present iff the attribute was declared via a named timeline; a Characteristic's facet is CharacteristicTimelineFacet, which has no such field.

CharacteristicTimelineFacet.description: The TimelineFacet of a Characteristic (IR-SPEC ch. 2.2): the same node without 'timelineName'. v0 recorded no timeline name for a characteristic, so M1 keeps that position closed: an open one would be a wire field no producer writes and no reader checks. 'granularity' and 'count' are the attribute facet's own field schemas, by JSON pointer, so each is defined once, and 'fixedStart' is the timeline's (IR-SPEC ch. 2.8).

ParameterTimelineFacet.description: The TimelineFacet of a Parameter (IR-SPEC ch. 2.10): the same node without 'timelineName', for the reason CharacteristicTimelineFacet states: no parameter records a timeline name, so an open position would be a wire field no producer writes and no reader checks. 'granularity' and 'count' are the attribute facet's own field schemas, by JSON pointer, and 'fixedStart' is the timeline's (IR-SPEC ch. 2.8).

Domain.description: A named, reusable datatype (IR-SPEC ch. 2.3). The name is written once, here; the datatype at this declaration position carries no self-name (domainDatatype).

Parameter.description: A top-level named value (IR-SPEC ch. 2.10): its declared name, its datatype and, when it is time-dependent, its timeline facet (delta B18 of spec/proposals/V1-WIREMIGRATIE.md). The facet is ParameterTimelineFacet: no parameter records a timeline name, so the position is closed as a characteristic's is. Key order is this 'properties' order.

UnitSystem.description: A unit system (IR-SPEC ch. 2.5): its declared name and its units, as a list in declaration order. Each unit is written once, with its further spellings on the unit itself (Unit.spellings); there is no second map of spellings beside the units. Key order is this 'properties' order.

name.description: Extension field without semantics, like source: the name the source gives the block this default comes from; absent where it gives none (IR-SPEC ch. 6.1). No consumer may read a decision from it.

decision.description: Characteristic defaults only: attribute (true) or do-not-attribute (false); absent on attribute defaults.

justification.description: The justification; absent only on the initialisation default (its justification is input-emptiness, ch. 7.3) and on a group-default (ch. 7.9).

consequence.description: Attribute defaults only: the default's value; a leeg-evaluating consequence falls through.

initialisation.description: The initialisation default (lowest only): justified iff the target is empty in the input facts.

unordered.description: Declared-unordered (ch. 7.9): two or more exception groups require this marking, the root regime applied at every level; a differing-deciding exception group propagates the conflict to the root (WF-075).

exceptions.description: Extension field (v1, Phase 5c): the nested exception groups of RUNTIME-SEMANTICS ch. 7.9 — a default's exception slot as a rose tree. A default carrying exceptions is either a group-default (no own decision/consequence — its exception groups are its decision, carrying a multi-member base or exception group as a chain position) or a form-a default (own decision/consequence too — the exception groups decide first, its own consequence the fall-back when they decide nothing). The initialisation and input defaults are root-only. Never emitter-produced.

statuteAnnotations.description: Extension field without semantics, like source and name (IR-SPEC ch. 6.1): the statute annotations written directly above the block this default comes from, one opaque string per annotation line, in source order — the field a Rule carries (ch. 3.1). When present a non-empty list of non-empty strings, absent otherwise; that no entry carries leading or trailing whitespace is WF-082's. No reader parses an entry.

defaults.description: One exception group — a member of a Default's exceptions: a default chain (descending, highest first) inheriting the root group's target, itself possibly nesting via Default.exceptions. Carries no target of its own.

ExceptionGroup.description: Extension node (v1, Phase 5c): one exception group — a member of a Default's exceptions (RUNTIME-SEMANTICS ch. 7.9). Never emitter-produced.

attribute.description: Attribute-defaults target; a group carries exactly one of characteristic/attribute (WF-050).

unordered.description: Declared-unordered (ch. 7.2): multiple defaults groups on one target are admissible iff every one carries this marking; differing simultaneous decisions route to the §9.5 channel.

PrioritizedDefaults.description: Extension node (v1, Phase 4): the prioritized-defaults group — defaults in descending priority; the highest default that decides wins. Characteristic target: decision (true = attribute, false = do-not-attribute); attribute target: consequence (a leeg-evaluating consequence falls through); the initialisation default (lowest) is justified iff the target is empty in the input.

fixedStart.description: The point the periods run from (IR-SPEC ch. 2.8): a date 'yyyy-mm-dd' on a week grid or a grid of count 2 or more, a day-month '--mm-dd' on a month, quarter or year grid of count 1; absent = the calendar grid, or a variable start. Written whole or not at all, never null. Which lexeme the grid takes, that it names a day of the calendar, the canonical month, the refusal of '--01-01', of a start on a variable-start timeline and of a facet that does not adopt its timeline's are WF-115, a verifier rule with its own witnesses, so the schema admits any string here, as it admits any integer as a count.

DayKind.description: A day kind (IR-SPEC ch. 2.9): its singular 'name' and its optional 'plural', the spelling it takes as a duration unit. These two are every spelling a day kind has on the wire; WF-017 holds them against the calendar spellings and against the other day kinds'. Key order is this 'properties' order.

formName.description: The name of a named form (IR-SPEC ch. 3, Versioning), written once, on the form. Nullable: a name that is absent or blank is WF-107's, a verifier rule with its own witnesses. A name ending in a space, '#' and digits cannot be written: that is the spelling of one version of a form with several (delta B19), on the v0 wire and in the in-memory records of the readers, so a form carrying it would read as a version of another. The pattern is written with [\s\S] and a lookahead, not '.' and '$', so that ECMA-262's search and a full match agree on it (gate 2).

statuteAnnotations.description: Extension field (IR-SPEC ch. 3.1): the statute annotations written above the rule header, on the form, one list for all its versions. When present a non-empty list of non-empty strings, absent otherwise; that no entry carries leading or trailing whitespace is WF-082's.

Rule.description: A rule (IR-SPEC ch. 3.1): one name, its versions in declaration order (delta B19).

RuleVersion.description: One version of a Rule (IR-SPEC ch. 3.1), without a node discriminator: a version is part of its form. 'validity' is always written; a Validity with neither bound is always. 'target' is an attribute reference, and whether it names an attribute or a characteristic is its declaration's (delta B20). 'initialisation' is always written. 'presentation' is the dialect tag of a computing version and never stands beside initialisation true; which member kind each combination writes is WF-022's. An absent condition is unconditional.

ObjectCreation.description: An object creation (IR-SPEC ch. 3.3): one name, its versions in declaration order (delta B19).

connectingRole.description: Extension field (wire-entry discipline, IR-SPEC Method): the created-side role of the back-link, named explicitly; required where the type-pair derivation is role-ambiguous (a self-typed pair). Absent, the back-link is derived (RUNTIME-SEMANTICS ch. 5.5). Written whole or not at all, never null.

ObjectCreationVersion.description: One version of an ObjectCreation (IR-SPEC ch. 3.3), without a node discriminator. 'subject' is nullable because WF-034 holds its presence; each initialisation is a MemberInit.

Allocation.description: An allocation (IR-SPEC ch. 3.2): one name, its versions in declaration order (delta B19).

connectingRole.description: The recipient relation: the connecting fact type with the role the targetType instances fill bound. Required: the allocation's relation is written, never derived (delta B12; CONSTRUCTS row 4).

AllocationVersion.description: One version of an Allocation (IR-SPEC ch. 3.2), without a node discriminator. 'method' is one of the three real methods: the v0 placeholder for an unhandled form cannot be written. The four type and attribute fields are nullable because WF-034 holds their presence; an absent optional attribute field is none, an empty string stays WF-034's.

Consistency.description: A consistency rule (IR-SPEC ch. 3.5): one name, its versions in declaration order (delta B19).

ConsistencyVersion.description: One version of a Consistency (IR-SPEC ch. 3.5), without a node discriminator. 'subject' is nullable because WF-029 holds its presence. 'source' is the version's source record; on a consistency version it carries the line of the source text as well.

Uniqueness.description: A uniqueness rule (IR-SPEC ch. 3.6): one name, its versions in declaration order (delta B19); one construct for the single-type and the union form (delta B27).

scope.description: The scope-parent role of a parent-scoped uniqueness, named symbolically: the bound role is the role the scope hop reaches (its filler is the scope parent). Its presence IS the scoping: a uniqueness without it is unscoped (B8). Only a single-source uniqueness carries it: a scoped union is an open design question (IR-SPEC ch. 3.6). Written whole or not at all, never null.

UniquenessVersion.description: One version of a Uniqueness (IR-SPEC ch. 3.6), without a node discriminator. One source is the single-type form, two or more the union; that the sources agree on key arity and kind is WF-030's. 'source' is the version's source record.

Source.description: One source of a Uniqueness (IR-SPEC ch. 3.6): the object type and its key attributes, a multi-attribute key being jointly unique by positional concatenation. That the keys resolve is WF-030's.

FactCreation.description: A fact creation (IR-SPEC ch. 3.4): one name, its versions in declaration order (delta B19).

path.description: How the targets are reached from the anchor: one RoleBinding per hop, in order, the last being the hop that reaches the target type.

FactCreationVersion.description: One version of a FactCreation (IR-SPEC ch. 3.4), without a node discriminator. The target type is not written: it is the declared filler of targetRole in factType. A step of the path is the role binding itself, with no node around it.

Diagnostic.description: The producer's own account of what stayed unresolved in a document it did write (WF-113). 'severity' is warning only: a severity error means the producer refused to write the document, and info is not a wire severity. A 'message' that is neither empty nor blank, a 'line' of at least 0 (0 = no source position, a hand-built document) and the accounting of every Unresolved node are verifier checks (WF-113), so 'line' admits any integer here.

Vocabulary.description: A named vocabulary (IR-SPEC ch. 2.12): the set of designations, at most one per declaration, that a consumer can speak instead of the declared names. 'name' is what every Designation names it by; 'default' marks the vocabulary that names every designatable declaration, at most one per document (WF-116, WF-119); 'language' is a language code, absent when none is declared. A vocabulary has no kind: every designation is text (maintainer decision 2026-09-27), and whether a vocabulary's designations can serve as identifiers is its consumer's question. What a name and a language code may spell is the verifier's (WF-116): the schema carries no pattern. Key order is this 'properties' order.

designations.description: Extension field (IR-SPEC ch. 2.12): the designations of one declaration, at most one per vocabulary (WF-117). Written whole or not at all: absent when the declaration carries none, and when present at least one. It stands last on every node that carries it — ObjectType, Attribute, Characteristic, FactType, Role, Parameter, the named forms (Rule, Allocation, ObjectCreation, FactCreation, Consistency, Uniqueness, PrioritizedDefaults) and RuleGroup — and an enumeration value's stand in its domain's 'valueDesignations'. A side table without semantics: every reader reads it structurally, and none reads it for evaluation.

Origin.description: Extension field (IR-SPEC ch. 2.13): the origin of a declaration a producer made itself, under a name no source declares — the form that made it and the declaration it comes from. Written whole or not at all, and only on such a declaration. It stands just before 'designations' on every node that may carry those (ObjectType, Attribute, Characteristic, FactType, Role, Parameter, the named forms and RuleGroup). The values of 'form' are layer: dialect(regelspraak), the record is layer: core. A side table without semantics: every reader reads it structurally, and none reads it for evaluation; whether 'from' names a declaration of its kind, comes back to the declaration that carries it, or fits its form is the verifier's (WF-121): the schema cannot cross a name with a declaration. Key order is this 'properties' order.

OriginSource.description: The declaration a made declaration comes from (IR-SPEC ch. 2.13), by name as every reference of the format: its kind, the declaration that scopes it ('owner': the object type that declares an attribute or a characteristic, the fact type of a role, the domain of an enumeration value; absent for every other kind, WF-121 (b)) and its canonical name. The kind 'decisionTable' names a decision table of the RegelSpraak dialect, which is no declaration on the wire: its rows are. Key order is this 'properties' order.

Designation.description: One designation (IR-SPEC ch. 2.12): the name of the declaration that carries it in the vocabulary 'vocabulary', which names a declared Vocabulary. A designation is text — not empty, trimmed, without a parenthesis — and that, like the uniqueness of the effective names in a vocabulary (WF-118), is the verifier's (WF-117): the schema cannot cross a designation with the vocabulary it names. Key order is this 'properties' order.

ValueDesignation.description: One designation of an enumeration value (IR-SPEC ch. 2.12): 'value' names one of the values of the Enumeration it stands beside (WF-117), 'vocabulary' and 'designation' as on a Designation. Key order is this 'properties' order.
